passage_text: Researchers studied the effect of varying doses of a novel cognitive enhancer on reaction time in healthy adults. Participants were randomly assigned to one of four groups: Control (placebo), Low Dose (10 mg), Medium Dose (20 mg), and High Dose (40 mg). Each participant completed a computerized simple reaction time task, and mean response times were recorded. The study aimed to determine whether increasing doses would produce a dose‑response relationship in reaction time improvement. The data collected are summarized in Table 1 below, which includes mean response times and standard deviations for each group. The researchers hypothesized that higher doses would lead to faster reaction times, with the greatest improvement observed in the High Dose group.
table_data:
Group,Treatment,Mean Response Time (ms),Standard Deviation
Control,Placebo,350,15
Low Dose,10 mg,330,12
Medium Dose,20 mg,310,10
High Dose,40 mg,290,8
stem: According to Table 1, which group exhibited the fastest mean reaction time?
explanation: The High Dose group had the lowest mean response time of 290 ms, indicating the fastest reaction time among all groups.
trap: Students often select the Medium Dose (C) because it is the second‑highest dose, but the data show the High Dose has the fastest reaction time.

stem: Which variable is the independent variable in this experiment?
explanation: The independent variable is the factor that the experimenters manipulate, which in this case is the dose of the cognitive enhancer.
trap: Some students mistakenly choose mean reaction time (A) because it is the primary outcome measured, but it is the dependent variable.

stem: The study examined RT at four doses of a cognitive enhancer. Which pharmacological parameter is the concentration that produces 50% of the maximal effect on a dose–response curve?
explanation: EC50 is the concentration producing half of the maximal response and is a measure of potency. Kd is the ligand concentration at half receptor occupancy, LD50 is the dose lethal to half of subjects, and the therapeutic index is the ratio of toxic to effective dose.
trap: Confusing Kd (binding) with EC50 (functional response); they coincide only when there is no signal amplification.
